entities.summary:
Bentivenga dei Bentivenghi, O. Min., also written Bentivenga de Bentivengis or Bentivegna de' Bentivegni, was an Italian Franciscan and cardinal born around 1225 in Siena, Tuscany, Italy. He was appointed as a bishop in 1255 and later became the Archbishop of Siena in 1277. Bentivenga played a significant role in the establishment of the Franciscan Order in Italy and was instrumental in the translation of numerous religious texts into the vernacular. He died on April 1, 1289, in Perugia, Umbria, Italy.

Bentivenga's significance lies in his efforts to promote the Franciscan ideals of poverty, simplicity, and devotion to the Eucharist. He also worked to strengthen the Franciscan Order's presence in Italy and Europe. His legacy can be seen in the many monasteries and churches he founded, including the Basilica of San Francesco in Assisi.

The translation of religious texts into the vernacular during Bentivenga's lifetime had a profound impact on the spread of Christianity in Europe. This movement, known as the ' vernacularization of Christianity', enabled the faithful to access and understand religious texts in their native languages, leading to a deeper connection with their faith.

Bentivenga's contributions to the Franciscan Order also led to the establishment of the 'studium generale' – a centralized institution that coordinated the Order's activities and provided a unified framework for its members. This institution played a crucial role in the dissemination of Franciscan teachings and practices across Europe.
